entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The degree to which a plan specifies what action will occur, when, where, how, and with what resources.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC114; SRC155.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Reduces translation ambiguity and supports preparation, cue recognition, and coordination.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Action Plan Specificity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Persists while the goal remains valued and feasible; may decay or be revised after feedback.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater plan specificity and completeness.
entities.representationScale: Vague–specific; coded completeness of action elements

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The currently available capacity to direct, sustain, or shift attention according to goals despite distraction or threat.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC148; SRC149.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Protects task-relevant processing and limits capture by distractors or worry.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Attentional Control Capacity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater goal-directed control of attention.
entities.representationScale: Low–high control; interference or switching performance

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The capacity to vary coping strategies in response to changing demands, controllability, and feedback.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC121; SRC143.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Improves regulation by matching strategy to situational demands rather than rigidly repeating one response.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Coping Strategy Flexibility
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater ability to adapt coping strategy to context.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The currently available capacity to modify the intensity, duration, expression, or consequences of emotion in service of goals.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC121; SRC143; SRC144.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Changes how strongly emotion constrains attention, valuation, communication, and action.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Emotion Regulation Capacity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater capacity to alter emotion or its consequences effectively.
entities.representationScale: Low–high capacity; strategy-success rating; task performance

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The strength and accessibility of a commitment linking a specified situational cue to a specified goal-directed response.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC114; SRC120; SRC155.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Makes the cue more accessible and delegates response initiation to the cue when the underlying goal is active.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Implementation Intention Strength
entities.persistenceRecovery: Persists while the goal remains valued and feasible; may decay or be revised after feedback.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = stronger cue–response commitment in service of an active goal.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The currently available capacity to suppress or stop a dominant, prepotent, or already initiated response.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC149; SRC186.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Permits goals and rules to override impulses or automatic responses.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Response Inhibition Capacity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater ability to suppress the specified response.
entities.representationScale: Low–high capacity; stop-signal or go/no-go performance

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The currently available capacity to align behavior with valued longer-term goals when immediate impulses or competing responses are present.

entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Supports inhibition, attention, and strategy deployment when immediate and longer-term goals conflict.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Self-Control Capacity
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater current capacity for goal-consistent restraint.
entities.representationScale: Low–high state capacity; behavioral restraint index

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating self-regulatory failure as a fixed personal deficit when task demands, opportunity, goals, or fatigue may dominate.
entities.definition: The frequency and attentional intensity with which a person observes and compares their behavior or progress against a target.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC139; SRC109.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Planning and regulation scales; executive-control tasks; diary or experience sampling; behavioral performance measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Performance tasks and self-report capture different facets; capacity can be distinguished from momentary deployment and opportunity.
entities.mechanism: Makes discrepancies visible and enables feedback-driven adjustment.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Cognitive load, fatigue, stress, task complexity, cue availability, motivation, and plan quality.
entities.name: Self-Monitoring Intensity

entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = more frequent or intensive monitoring.
entities.representationScale: Checks per period; low–high monitoring frequency/intensity
